title: Deep-learning-based single-domain and multidomain protein structure prediction with D-I-TASSER
one_line: Zhang-lab pipeline D-I-TASSER combines deep-learning contact/distance restraints with I-TASSER-style threading and replica-exchange Monte Carlo folding, plus explicit domain splitting and domain assembly, to predict both single-domain and multidomain protein structures.
key_claims: Integrating multiple deep-learning spatial restraints into iterative threading-assembly simulations yields more accurate models than either the deep-learning predictors or the fragment-assembly pipeline alone on benchmark test sets.
Explicit domain boundary detection followed by individual domain modelling and domain assembly improves full-chain accuracy of multidomain proteins relative to whole-chain modelling.
The method was validated in blind CASP community assessment, where the automated D-I-TASSER server ranked among the top-performing structure prediction servers.
The authors applied the pipeline at proteome scale to human proteins, reporting structural models and domain-level annotations for sequences lacking experimental structures.
limitations: Podcast notes give only the DOI, so specific TM-score/GDT numbers, dataset sizes and baselines cannot be quoted here without checking the paper.
Physics-based replica-exchange simulation plus threading is far more compute-intensive per target than a single end-to-end network forward pass.
Accuracy still depends on MSA depth and on availability of useful structural templates, so orphan and fast-evolving sequences remain hard.
Domain assembly accuracy is bounded by correct domain boundary prediction; boundary errors propagate to the full-chain model.
Static single-conformation predictions say nothing about alternative states, complexes or ligand-bound forms.
open_questions: Head-to-head comparison with AlphaFold2/AlphaFold3-class predictors on a strictly held-out multidomain set, reporting full-chain and inter-domain accuracy separately.
How much of the gain comes from threading templates versus the deep-learning restraints, tested by ablation.
Whether improved inter-domain orientation accuracy translates into better downstream use, e.g. docking or function annotation.
Performance on targets with shallow MSAs and no homologous templates.
